summary: Preinstall dropper fetches Bun runtime and executes obfuscated bundled payload
details: package.json declares scripts.preinstall = "node setup.mjs". setup.mjs downloads the Bun runtime from github.com/oven-sh/bun releases and then invokes it via execFileSync to run a sibling file math_init.js. math_init.js is a ~727KB Bun-compiled JavaScript bundle (header `// @bun @bun-cjs`) using rotated string-array obfuscation (a WV8StW rotation function operating on a large hex-numeric constant array n7gIxM, with mangled identifiers), so its code is not readable by Node-based scanners. The advertised package is a trivial ESLint processors stub — dist/index.js is roughly five lines — so the Bun runtime and the large obfuscated payload have no relationship to the declared function. The package is published under the @servicetitan scope and points repository at servicetitan/uikit, but ships this preinstall dropper alongside the stub, matching a scope-impersonation delivery of an install-time payload. On npm install the obfuscated bundle executes automatically on the installer's machine under a fetched second runtime that bypasses Node-visible inspection.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
